extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and practitioners facing USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO, and the requirements/effects of an affidavit of resignation leading to exclusion on consent (including publication and reinstatement presumptions). Useful for evaluating practitioner compliance and preparing or responding to OED disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation / Exclusion on Consent (37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent submitted an Affidavit of Resignation pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 to be excluded on consent. The Director determined the affidavit complied with § 11.27(a) and approved it, resulting in exclusion on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit must be freely and voluntarily rendered and the practitioner must fully understand the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion. If accepted, the practitioner is excluded on consent effective as ordered; the OED Director will publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and issue a materially consistent Official Gazette notice. The affidavit's statements may carry presumptions for any future reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve exclusion (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D), 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's approval is the operative act effecting exclusion on consent; procedural compliance with cited statutes and regulations is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform client of Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not fail to inform a client or former client of correspondence received from the Office that could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision describes multiple instances where the practitioner received Office notices (e.g., non‑final Office actions, notices of defective declaration, Notices of Abandonment) and did not provide them to the client — an example of violating this rule. Keeping clients informed of substantive Office correspondence is required; failure may support discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) / 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice; such conduct is professional misconduct under § 11.804(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director concluded certain omissions (e.g., not informing clients, not replying to Office notices) were the basis for an opinion that the practitioner engaged in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice. Examples: allowing applications to become abandoned without notifying clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) / 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office; such conduct is professional misconduct under § 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED may view repeated failures in communication, diligence, or honesty as reflecting adversely on fitness to practice. The Final Order treats these standards collectively when assessing misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of a legal matter (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not neglect a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the order: failing to respond to Office notices (leading to abandonment), failing to pursue prosecution or inform clients of abandonment, and failing to return client funds for unperformed services. Neglect can include not taking required steps after leaving employment (e.g., not changing correspondence address or withdrawing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by client's decisions and consult as to means (37 C.F.R. § 11.102(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall abide by a client's decisions concerning the objectives of representation and shall consult with the client as to the means by which they are to be pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must obtain client input on objectives and consult about how to achieve them; failing to consult or to keep the client informed undermines this obligation (illustrated by facts where clients were not told about rejections or abandonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites failure to timely reply to Office notices and prolonged lack of communication as examples inconsistent with this duty. Demonstrable timely action on Office communications and client matters is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable consultation and communication (37 C.F.R. § 11.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished, keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter, promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client, consult with the client about any relevant limitation on the practitioner's conduct and explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific failures cited include not informing clients of Office rejections, Notices of Abandonment, or options for further prosecution; not providing client files; and misleading or incomplete status updates. Adequate, timely, and truthful communication is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation regarding scope of representation and fees (37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall consult with the client regarding the scope of the representation and the basis or rate of the fee and expenses for which the client will be responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The facts include a fee-for-service ('patent acceleration review') where work was not performed and funds were not returned — illustrating the importance of clear fee/scope consultation and appropriate handling of client funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safekeeping client property (37 C.F.R. § 11.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule setting forth a practitioner's duties in safekeeping property of a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not elaborated in detail in this order, the rule is cited among those the OED Director believed were violated; practitioners must properly handle and account for client funds and property (e.g., return unearned funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties when terminating representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule setting forth a practitioner's duties in terminating a representation of a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes the practitioner did not file a request to withdraw and did not change correspondence address after leaving employment; proper termination/withdrawal procedures and client notice are required to avoid harm to client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the order: telling a client a petition had been filed when it had not, giving misleading status reports, or other misrepresentations about filings or case status. Such actions can form the basis for professional misconduct findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct definitions and catch‑alls (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) and (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (§ 11.804(d)) or other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness (§ 11.804(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions are invoked in conjunction with more specific duties (communication, diligence, honesty) to characterize various failures as professional misconduct; they operate as broader categories for sanctionable behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumptions and compliance with reinstatement rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.60; § 11.58, § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: By consenting to exclusion, the respondent acknowledged that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for reinstatement determination that (a) the facts in the OED file are true and (b) he could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners who accept exclusion on consent should understand that the factual findings in the OED file will be conclusively presumed at reinstatement and must comply fully with §§ 11.58 (duties following disciplinary action), 11.59, and 11.60 on any reinstatement request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office publication and notice requirements upon exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion on consent will be publicly posted; the Official Gazette notice must set out the practitioner identity, registration number, nature of action, the rules alleged violated, and the fact that the practitioner voluntarily submitted the affidavit while an investigation was pending and did not admit violations but accepted presumptions for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner responsibilities upon leaving employment (implicit under communication/termination rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a practitioner leaves employment, the practitioner must ensure clients are informed, change correspondence addresses as appropriate, take steps to withdraw as attorney of record if no longer representing the client, and preserve client interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order records failures: practitioner left employer, did not change correspondence address, did not withdraw, and did not communicate with clients — resulting in abandonments and lack of client knowledge. These facts illustrate the application of § 11.104 and § 11.116 to transitions of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to respond to Office communications to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must reply to Office notices (e.g., notices of defective declaration or Office actions) within prescribed times (e.g., two months, extendable) or take proper steps to avoid abandonment of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order recounts notices that required replies to avoid abandonment; failing to provide notices to the client or to reply led to abandonment. Timely handling of Office deadlines and client notification are required to preserve client rights.
